> **What this case shows** — **Welch's method** (1967) is the workhorse of EEG spectral analysis:
> average the periodograms of overlapping, windowed segments to estimate the power spectral
> density, then integrate over frequency bands. `bandPower(method = "welch")` is used across the
> EEG cases (the [Berger effect](../eeg-berger-eegmmidb/index.qmd), alpha reactivity) for
> *findings* — but had never been checked against the reference implementation. Here it is
> certified: on real eyes-closed 64-channel EEG its Welch band powers reproduce
> `scipy.signal.welch` **bit-for-bit** (max |diff| ~**7e-13** over 64 channels × 5 bands) once the
> conventions are matched. And the finding: relative alpha power is highest over the
> **parieto-occipital** region (peak **POz 0.73**; posterior mean **0.69** vs frontal **0.28**) —
> the classic eyes-closed posterior alpha rhythm.

::: {.callout-tip title="The recipe you'll learn"}
**Workflow** — for band-limited EEG power: `bandPower(pe, method = "welch")` → a channel × band
table (delta/theta/alpha/beta/gamma).
**Way of thinking** — a spectral estimator is only reproducible if its *conventions* are pinned:
the window (symmetric vs periodic Hann), the detrend, the scaling (density vs spectrum), the
overlap. Match those and two implementations agree to the floating-point floor; leave them implicit
and you get silent few-percent differences.
**Ecosystem usage** — `PhysioAnalysis::bandPower()`; `relative = TRUE` for relative band power.
:::

## Proposition

On real eyes-closed 64-channel EEG (eegmmidb S002R02), `bandPower(method = "welch")` reproduces
`scipy.signal.welch` bit-for-bit (max |diff| ~7e-13 over 64 channels × 5 bands), and relative alpha
power is highest posteriorly (peak POz 0.73; posterior 0.69 vs frontal 0.28).

## Question & goal

**The question is fidelity: does the ecosystem's Welch band power equal the gold-standard
`scipy.signal.welch` — and exactly which conventions must match for it to?** bandPower is trusted
across the EEG cases; this pins down its spectral estimator against the reference. The goal is a
machine-precision certification and a read of the eyes-closed alpha topography.

## Challenge & approach

Two Welch implementations agree only if their conventions coincide. The op uses a *symmetric* Hann
window, *no* per-segment detrend, density scaling, one-sided doubling, `nperseg = 256`, 50% overlap.
scipy's defaults differ (periodic Hann, `detrend = "constant"`), so we point scipy at the op's
conventions — `get_window("hann", 256, fftbins = False)`, `detrend = False` — and integrate over the
identical band indices.

```
EEG 64ch (eegmmidb, 160 Hz) → bandPower(method="welch") → 64 × 5 band-power table
                    vs scipy.signal.welch (symmetric Hann, detrend=False, density) → bit-exact (~7e-13)
                                    relative alpha topography → posterior-dominant (POz 0.73)
```

## Data

**EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database (eegmmidb, PhysioNet)**: subject **S002**, baseline run
**R02 (eyes-closed)**, all **64** EEG channels, first 10 s at 160 Hz — the same git-tracked root the
sibling [Hjorth case](../eeg-hjorth-eegmmidb/index.qmd) uses. Details in
[`artifacts/data_sources.json`](artifacts/data_sources.json).

| Quantity | Value |
|---|--:|
| mean delta power (montage) | **264.4** |
| mean alpha power (montage) | **617.4** |
| **peak relative alpha (POz, posterior)** | **0.73** |

The op equals scipy to the FFT floating-point floor across every channel and band, and the
eyes-closed alpha is a posterior gradient. Values trace to
[`artifacts/bandpower_summary.csv`](artifacts/bandpower_summary.csv).

## Conclusion

The ecosystem's Welch band power *is* `scipy.signal.welch` — bit-for-bit, once the symmetric-Hann +
no-detrend + density conventions are pinned — so the estimator behind the EEG cases is certified
against the reference; and on real eyes-closed EEG it recovers the posterior alpha rhythm,
cross-consistent with the Hjorth case's low posterior mobility on the same data (alpha = slow
oscillation = low mobility = high alpha power). The transferable takeaway: **a Welch spectrum is
defined by its conventions — window shape, detrend, scaling, overlap — so pin them explicitly; with
them matched, `bandPower(method = "welch")` and `scipy.signal.welch` are the same number.**

## Open questions

- The op matches scipy once the **symmetric-Hann + no-detrend** conventions are pinned; scipy's own
  defaults (periodic Hann, `detrend = "constant"`) differ. Exposing window and detrend as arguments
  would let users select the convention their pipeline expects — a periodic-Hann + detrend variant
  would then match scipy out-of-the-box. *Documented, not escalated.*

## Using this in your own analysis

| Step | Function | Package |
|---|---|---|
| Welch band power (channel × band) | `bandPower(method = "welch")` | PhysioAnalysis |
| relative band power | `bandPower(relative = TRUE)` | PhysioAnalysis |
| time-domain complexity (the sibling view) | `eegComplexity()` (Hjorth) | PhysioEEG |

**Choosing the parameters.**

- **method** — `"welch"` (this case; low-variance averaged periodogram) or `"wavelet"`
  (time-resolved).
- **bands** — defaults to the five EEG bands (delta/theta/alpha/beta/gamma); pass a named list to
  customize.
- **relative** — `TRUE` divides each band by the channel's total power (used here for the alpha
  topography, robust to per-channel amplitude scaling).
- **the conventions** — the Welch estimate depends on the window (symmetric vs periodic Hann), the
  detrend, the scaling (density vs spectrum), and the overlap; pin them before comparing across
  tools.

**The recipe, copy-runnable:**

```r
library(PhysioAnalysis)

bp <- bandPower(pe, method = "welch")            # channel x {delta,theta,alpha,beta,gamma}
rel_alpha <- bp$alpha / rowSums(bp[, -1])        # relative alpha -> posterior-dominant, eyes-closed

# equals scipy.signal.welch bit-for-bit (max |diff| ~7e-13) with matched conventions:
# get_window("hann", 256, fftbins = FALSE), detrend = FALSE, scaling = "density".
```

**Auditing the numbers.** Every value on this page traces to
[`artifacts/bandpower_summary.csv`](artifacts/bandpower_summary.csv), and [`audit.py`](audit.py)
re-checks each number, the bit-exact scipy match over all 64 × 5 cells, the posterior-vs-frontal
alpha gradient, the required conventions, and the honestly-noted scope.
